thread:
elaine_sales: Heads-up — Pioneer wants a Private deployment POC next week. They want inference inside their VPC via PrivateLink or peering. Security says they need static egress IPs and SNI preserved for their downstream TLS-inspect boxes. Any immediate blockers or things I should ask them? cc @mike_netops @omar_security

mike_netops: Quick Q — do they require full control over egress (i.e., customer-managed NAT) or do they expect Redwood Private to supply static egress IPs? Also: are they ok with an NLB-based PrivateLink endpoint? that implies the endpoint IPs are our NLBs and we generally terminate behind an NLB.

omar_security: Two things to call out: 1) SNI is visible in the TLS ClientHello unless they use ESNI. If they do TLS inspection, SNI will be available to their appliance. 2) Preserving original client source IP across PrivateLink + NLB is non-trivial — NLBs will appear as source. If they absolutely need source preservation for firewall rules, we can offer a proxy mode or ask them to peer and route through their NAT.

jess_solutions: For the POC I usually recommend PrivateLink + Dedicated capacity: simpler security model and we can provide a stable set of egress IPs from the Dedicated VPC. Pricing note: Dedicated/Private has a platform package + reserved capacity commit. POC sized for 1-2 GPUs for 2 weeks is typically quoted as a short-term reserved commit (we can convert to usage after). I can draft a rough estimate once we confirm capacity and expected token throughput.

mike_netops: Minimal firewall checklist I ask customers for — can share with Pioneer:
```
- Outbound TCP 443 to our PrivateLink NLB IP(s) (we'll provide exact /32s)
- Outbound DNS (UDP 53) to customer-configured resolver or allow egress to 8.8.8.8 if permitted
- If using webhooks/callbacks, allow inbound from our egress pool IPs (we'll provide)
```
If they choose VPC peering, we can preserve source IPs but they must accept route propagation and potentially asymmetric routing.

elaine_sales: Can you clarify the egress IP options and the timeline to provide the exact IP list? Pioneer is strict about firewall exceptions. Also they asked whether using PrivateLink will add latency or increase cost for POC.

omar_security: Egress options:
- Option A (recommended): Redwood-managed static egress IPs from Dedicated Private deployment. We provide a documented list of IPs (static) and rotate only with notice.
- Option B: Customer-managed NAT / proxy: the customer preserves source IP; they whitelist whatever IPs they want. More work on their side but preserves end-to-end identities.
- Option C: VPC peering: source IP preserved, but requires peering across accounts and route controls; note we need to confirm MTU/path and no overlapping CIDRs.

jess_solutions: Latency: PrivateLink adds one hop (NLB) and a couple ms in most regions — negligible for typical token-roundtrips. Cost: PrivateLink has NLB+data transfer costs; Dedicated capacity also has infra and commit pricing. For short POC we can waive some setup fees — I'll check.

deploy-bot: pcp-request created: POC-1767777777 — engineering onboarding ticket opened (opt-in for dedicated capacity).

mike_netops: One more practical snippet for the customer's firewall team:
```
# example firewall rule for POC
ALLOW tcp 443 to 203.0.113.45/32  # Redwood PrivateLink NLB (example)
ALLOW udp 53 to 10.0.0.2/32       # DNS resolver inside customer's VPC (if used)
```
I'll need their CIDR ranges and whether they will accept EFIP-based whitelisting or need NAT passthrough.

elaine_sales: Awesome — I'll send this checklist to the customer and ask: (1) do you prefer Redwood-managed static egress or will you run NAT/proxy? (2) confirm CIDR ranges and TLS-inspect requirements (SNI visible?) (3) any compliance blockers for NLB endpoints. Can we get final IP list by EOD tomorrow? :thumbsup:

omar_security: We'll provision a provisional IP list for the POC by EOD tomorrow. If Pioneer requires HSM/KMS integration notes or SOC/ISO docs, ping me and I'll attach the compliance pack.

elaine_sales: Thanks everyone — I'll update Pioneer and loop back with their reply.
